rows.label: Fed funds rate
rows.meaning: The overnight rate the Fed sets.

rows.label: 2-year Treasury
rows.meaning: Where markets expect Fed policy over the next two years.

rows.label: 10-year Treasury
rows.why: long rates are high, pressuring valuations
rows.meaning: The long rate behind mortgages and stock valuations.

rows.label: 10-year real yield
rows.meaning: The 10-year yield after expected inflation (TIPS).

rows.label: Yield curve (10y − 3m)
rows.meaning: Below zero (inverted) has preceded every US recession since 1968.

rows.label: Core CPI, year on year
rows.meaning: Consumer prices excluding food and energy.

rows.label: Core PCE, year on year
rows.meaning: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge; target 2%.

rows.label: Headline CPI, year on year
rows.meaning: All consumer prices.

rows.label: 5-year inflation expectation
rows.meaning: Inflation the bond market expects over five years.

rows.label: Unemployment rate
rows.meaning: Share of the labor force without a job.

rows.label: Sahm recession indicator
rows.meaning: Rise in the 3-month unemployment average above its 12-month low; 0.5 has marked recessions.

rows.label: Jobs added per month (3-mo avg)
rows.meaning: Average monthly change in payrolls over three months.

rows.label: Weekly jobless claims
rows.meaning: New unemployment filings, the fastest layoff signal.

rows.label: Real GDP growth (annualized)
rows.meaning: Inflation-adjusted output, latest quarter.

rows.label: Industrial production, y/y
rows.meaning: Factory, mining and utility output.

rows.label: Retail sales, y/y
rows.meaning: Consumer spending at stores and online, not inflation-adjusted.

rows.label: Consumer sentiment
rows.meaning: University of Michigan survey; 1966 = 100.

rows.label: High-yield credit spread
rows.meaning: Extra yield on junk bonds over Treasuries; FRED publishes only the last 3 years.

rows.label: Corporate credit spread (Baa − 10y)
rows.meaning: Extra yield on investment-grade corporate bonds; history since 1986.

rows.label: Financial conditions (NFCI)
rows.meaning: Chicago Fed index; above 0 is tighter than average.

rows.label: Fed balance sheet, y/y
rows.meaning: Fed asset holdings; shrinking is quantitative tightening.

rows.label: Money supply (M2), y/y
rows.meaning: Cash, deposits and money-market funds.

rows.label: Broad dollar, y/y
rows.meaning: The dollar against major trading partners.

rows.label: WTI crude oil
rows.why: oil is high enough to squeeze consumers
rows.meaning: US oil price, monthly average.
